channel.title: Comments for page "Dimensions 2, 3, and Onward"
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Dimensions 2, 3, and Onward"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Why do you do this to me? You give 507 a true name and an amazing girl, give Cassie a real body, have them hold hands in a meadow, and then KILL THEM! My heart!

This was obviously very well done, and I love it to bits. 507 will never just be 507 to me anymore. He’s John, the guy who’s insecure about his “boring” nature (compared to everyone else in the foundation) and gets flustered around ladies. And also hops between dimensions.

+1. Great job!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Oof this hurt me. Well written, gave me the slightest bit of hope before it was mercilessly crushed into oblivion. +1

item.content:encoded:
I think this is one of the scariest articles I've read on the entire site.

Cassy (I will not call her 085) always brings a smile to my face, and the characterization of 507 was really clever, but seeing them essentially die in this manner is more frightening (and heart-wrenching) than most of the horror I've read on the site.

Damn. You really yanked the rug out from us in the end there.

+1. Excellent characterization of two older SCP articles.

item.content:encoded: The characterization here is phenomenal, and I like how it builds upon Kaktus' 2nd proposal. I really want to see more old scips framed with the standards of Series IV now. +1

This is honestly one of the better things that’s come out of this contest. I love how you personified SCP-507, and it’s great how you used Cassie in this.

+1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Holy shit.

Like, I love 507, it was one of the first skips I ever really latched onto as "my favorite", but it's so bad compared to what it could be by today's standards. So to see someone using him seriously is great.

And like… This was really cute? Up until it was tragic and horrifying, anyway. But that final line was fucking perfect. I have zero idea what was going on for any of this, but I loved every second of it. +1
